issues.description: PCI DSS violation: Storing raw credit card numbers, CVV, and expiry dates in application memory and potentially logs. This violates PCI compliance requirements which mandate that full card data must never be stored or logged.
issues.suggestion: Remove cardNumber, expiryDate, and cvv fields from PaymentDetails interface. Use a PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal) that returns a payment token. Replace with: { paymentToken: string; amount: number; }

issues.description: Storing last four digits of card number in database without proper encryption or security controls. Even partial card data requires PCI compliance measures.
issues.suggestion: Do not store any card information directly. Use payment gateway webhooks to track payment status and reference transaction IDs from the gateway instead: await db.query(query, [transactionId, amount, 'completed'])

issues.description: Sensitive payment failure information logged to console, potentially exposing card data or payment details in logs.
issues.suggestion: Use structured, sanitized logging that excludes all payment details: logger.error('Payment processing failed', { userId, amount, errorCode: error.code })

issues.description: Card validation logic is insufficient and insecure. Luhn algorithm not implemented, allowing invalid card numbers. Storing and validating raw card data violates PCI DSS.
issues.suggestion: Remove all card validation logic from application. Delegate to PCI-compliant payment gateway: async function processPayment(userId: string, paymentToken: string, tier: string)

issues.description: Race condition in payment processing: If upgradeUserSubscription fails after chargeCard succeeds, user is charged but not upgraded. No transaction rollback or idempotency handling.
issues.suggestion: Implement idempotent payment processing with database transactions or use payment gateway webhooks: Begin transaction -> charge card -> upgrade subscription -> commit. On failure, initiate refund via payment gateway.

issues.description: Price calculation happens before charging, but payment.amount is validated against calculated amount. An attacker could manipulate the client to send correct amount but have tier changed afterward.
issues.suggestion: Calculate price server-side only and never trust client-provided amount: Remove payment.amount from interface, calculate server-side, and pass calculated amount to payment gateway.

issues.description: Silent failure when payment.amount < calculated amount. Returns false without logging security event, making it easy to miss fraud attempts.
issues.suggestion: Log security events and throw error: if (payment.amount < amount) { logger.security('Payment amount mismatch', { userId, expected: amount, received: payment.amount }); throw new Error('Payment amount validation failed'); }

issues.description: Pricing calculation has precision issues with floating-point arithmetic. 9.99 * 0.08 * 0.029 can result in rounding errors, potentially undercharging or overcharging customers.
issues.suggestion: Use integer arithmetic (cents) or a decimal library: Use Math.round(basePrice * 100) to work in cents, or import Decimal from 'decimal.js' and calculate: new Decimal(basePrice).times(TAX_RATE).plus(new Decimal(basePrice).times(PROCESSING_FEE)).plus(basePrice).toNumber()

issues.description: Date comparison for expiry validation uses current month, but credit cards are typically valid through the last day of the expiry month. A card expiring '12/25' would be rejected in December 2025 even though it's valid until Dec 31.
issues.suggestion: Set expiry date to last day of month: const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month), 0); // Day 0 = last day of previous month, so use parseInt(month) not parseInt(month) - 1

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability: features array is JSON.stringified and inserted directly without parameterization. PostgreSQL JSONB type should be used with proper parameterization.
issues.suggestion: Use proper JSONB type and parameterization: const query = 'INSERT INTO subscriptions (user_id, tier, valid_until, features) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4::jsonb) ON CONFLICT...' and pass features array directly: await db.query(query, [userId, tier, validUntil, features])

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess does not handle expired subscriptions gracefully. Returns false but doesn't clean up expired subscription, leading to database bloat and potential billing issues.
issues.suggestion: Update subscription status when expired: if (validUntil < new Date()) { await db.query('UPDATE subscriptions SET tier = \'free\' WHERE user_id = $1', [userId]); return false; }

issues.description: JSON.parse on untrusted database data without try-catch. If features column contains invalid JSON, application crashes.
issues.suggestion: Add error handling: try { const features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); return features.includes(feature); } catch (error) { logger.error('Invalid subscription data', { userId }); return false; }

issues.description: Feature lists are hardcoded in upgradeUserSubscription function. When adding/removing features, must change code instead of configuration.
issues.suggestion: Extract to configuration: const TIER_FEATURES = { premium: ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes'], enterprise: [...] }; const features = TIER_FEATURES[tier];

issues.description: Card number validation only checks length === 16, but valid cards can be 13-19 digits (Amex is 15, some Visa are 13).
issues.suggestion: If card validation must be done (though it shouldn't per PCI), support multiple lengths: if (cardNumber.length < 13 || cardNumber.length > 19) { return false; }

issues.description: No validation that cardNumber contains only digits. Allows letters and special characters which could be used for injection attacks.
issues.suggestion: Validate format: if (!/^\d{13,19}$/.test(cardNumber)) { return false; }

issues.description: Tax rate and processing fee are hardcoded. Different jurisdictions have different tax rates, and payment processors charge different fees.
issues.suggestion: Move to configuration with regional support: const config = { taxRates: { US: 0.08, EU: 0.20 }, processingFee: 0.029 }; Pass userRegion to function and lookup appropriate tax rate.

issues.description: chargeCard function has no timeout or retry logic. If payment gateway is slow or fails transiently, payment fails permanently.
issues.suggestion: Add timeout and retry with exponential backoff: Use a payment library with built-in retry logic, or implement: const result = await retry(() => db.query(...), { retries: 3, timeout: 5000 });

issues.description: getUserSubscription returns null for non-existent subscriptions, but doesn't distinguish between 'no subscription' and 'database error'.
issues.suggestion: Add explicit error handling: if (rows.length === 0) { return { userId, tier: 'free', validUntil: new Date(), features: [] }; } to represent free tier explicitly.

issues.description: processPremiumPayment is doing too much: validation, pricing, payment, and subscription management. Violates Single Responsibility Principle.
issues.suggestion: Split into smaller functions: async function processPremiumPayment(userId, payment, tier) { const validatedPayment = await validateAndPreparePayment(payment, tier); const transaction = await chargePayment(validatedPayment); await upgradeSubscription(userId, tier, transaction.id); }

issues.description: Error messages are generic and not user-friendly. 'Invalid payment details' doesn't indicate which field failed validation.
issues.suggestion: Provide specific error messages: if (!validatePaymentDetails(payment)) { throw new Error('Payment validation failed: ${getValidationErrors(payment).join(', ')}'); }

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess makes a database query every time, even for frequently accessed features. No caching strategy.
issues.suggestion: Add caching layer: Use Redis or in-memory cache with TTL: const cacheKey = `subscription:${userId}`; const cached = await cache.get(cacheKey); if (cached) return JSON.parse(cached).features.includes(feature);

issues.description: Year 2000 assumption in date parsing (2000 + parseInt(year)) will break in 2100. While not immediate concern, shows poor future-proofing.
issues.suggestion: Use full year format or handle century correctly: const currentCentury = Math.floor(new Date().getFullYear() / 100) * 100; const fullYear = currentCentury + parseInt(year);

issues.description: File lacks comprehensive JSDoc comments for exported functions. Missing @param, @returns, @throws documentation.
issues.suggestion: Add complete JSDoc: /** * Processes premium subscription payment * @param userId - User identifier * @param payment - Payment token from gateway * @param tier - Subscription tier * @returns Promise resolving to payment success status * @throws {Error} On validation or payment failure */

issues.description: No audit logging for payment operations. Cannot track who processed payments, when, or detect fraud patterns.
issues.suggestion: Add audit trail: await auditLog.record({ event: 'payment_processed', userId, tier, amount, timestamp: new Date(), ip: requestIp });

codeQuality.summary: CRITICAL SECURITY VIOLATIONS: This code has severe PCI DSS compliance failures that make it illegal to deploy in production. Raw credit card data (cardNumber, CVV, expiryDate) is stored in memory and potentially logged, which violates payment card industry standards. The entire payment processing architecture must be redesigned to use a PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal, Square) that handles card data and returns tokens. Additional critical issues include race conditions in payment processing (charging card but failing to upgrade subscription), SQL injection vulnerabilities in JSON data handling, inadequate error handling, floating-point arithmetic errors in pricing calculations, and complete absence of tests for critical business logic. The code also has multiple high-severity bugs: incorrect card expiry validation, silent failures on payment amount mismatches, no transaction rollback mechanisms, and no fraud detection logging. This code should NOT be merged until payment processing is completely rewritten to delegate card handling to a certified payment processor and comprehensive tests are added.

Mock db.query to succeed. Assert function returns true and verify upgradeUserSubscription was called with correct parameters.

testCoverage.summary: CRITICAL COVERAGE GAP: The file src/premium.ts has ZERO test coverage for 190 lines of critical payment and subscription logic. This is a new file with no corresponding test file. Estimate: 0% coverage. The file contains 6 functions (3 exported, 3 internal) handling payment processing, card validation, pricing calculations, and subscription management. All functions are completely untested. Highest Priority Untested Paths: (1) Payment Processing (processPremiumPayment): No tests for the main payment flow including success path, validation failures, insufficient amounts, payment gateway failures, or database errors. Financial transactions without tests pose extreme risk. (2) Card Validation (validatePaymentDetails): No tests for credit card validation including card number length, CVV validation, expiry format, or expired card detection. Security-critical validation is completely untested. (3) Payment Execution (chargeCard): No tests for actual payment processing or database error handling. Could result in charging customers without service or granting service without payment. (4) Subscription Upgrade (upgradeUserSubscription): No tests for granting premium access after payment. Errors could cause payment without service. (5) Feature Access Control (hasFeatureAccess): No tests for controlling access to premium features, expired subscriptions, or users without subscriptions. Could allow unauthorized premium access. Recommendation: This PR should NOT be merged without comprehensive test coverage. At minimum, add tests for all critical paths (payment processing, card validation, feature access, pricing) before allowing this code into production.

refactorings.summary: The premium.ts file contains 10 significant refactoring opportunities focused on improving testability, maintainability, and type safety. Key improvements include: (1) extracting configuration constants for pricing and features, (2) separating validation logic into focused functions, (3) introducing custom error types for better error handling, (4) extracting SQL queries into named constants, (5) implementing dependency injection for the database client, and (6) adding branded types for sensitive payment data. High-impact changes center around database abstraction and error handling patterns, which will significantly improve testability. Medium-impact changes focus on breaking down complex functions and eliminating duplication. All suggestions preserve existing behavior while making the code more maintainable and test-friendly.

recommendations.description: BLOCKING ISSUE: The code violates PCI DSS compliance by handling raw credit card data (cardNumber, CVV, expiryDate) in application code. This is illegal for production deployment. Must integrate a PCI-compliant payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal, Square) that handles card data and returns payment tokens. Remove all card data handling from application code immediately.

BLOCKING ISSUE: The file has 0% test coverage for 190 lines of critical payment processing logic. No tests exist for payment flows, card validation, subscription management, or feature access control. This represents extreme financial and security risk. Add comprehensive test suite covering all critical paths before merge.

Race condition in payment processing: if upgradeUserSubscription fails after chargeCard succeeds, users are charged without receiving service. No transaction rollback or idempotency mechanisms exist. Implement proper transaction management with rollback capability or use payment gateway webhooks for atomic operations.

SQL injection vulnerability in JSON data handling. Features array is stringified and inserted without proper parameterization. Use PostgreSQL JSONB type with proper parameterization to prevent injection attacks.

Floating-point arithmetic errors in pricing calculations (line 96-109) can cause rounding errors in money calculations, potentially leading to undercharging or overcharging customers. Use integer arithmetic (cents) or a decimal library for all financial calculations.

Card expiry date validation incorrectly rejects cards that expire in the current month (line 82). Cards are valid through the last day of the expiry month. Fix date comparison logic to use end-of-month dates.

Database dependency is hard-coded throughout the file, making unit testing impossible without a real database. Implement dependency injection pattern to allow mock database injection during testing. This will enable comprehensive unit test coverage.

Pricing, tax rates, fees, and feature lists are hardcoded throughout the code. Extract these into centralized configuration constants at module level to improve maintainability and enable easy updates without code changes.

Generic Error types provide poor debugging information and make error handling difficult. Implement custom error classes (PaymentValidationError, InsufficientPaymentError, PaymentProcessingError) to enable specific error handling and better error messages.

SQL queries are scattered as inline strings throughout the file. Extract all SQL queries into named constants at module level to improve readability, enable query analysis, and facilitate security audits.
